applies_to: AAON DX barrel chillers with the Main DX Barrel Chiller Controller, up to two barrels and three refrigerant circuits per barrel, with optional pumping, WSE, evaporative condenser and vestibule modules.
summary: The Main DX Barrel Chiller Controller runs AAON DX chillers built with one or two barrel evaporators and has an on-board BACnet MS/TP port. The object map has 140 read-only analog inputs (water temperatures, pumping, WSE, evaporative condenser and per-circuit refrigerant data), 60 analog values (setpoints, calibration offsets, run command, relay and analog output overrides), 323 read-only binary inputs for status, faults, warnings and lockouts per circuit, and a multistate input for the unit mode.
notes: The guide gives no read/write column; AI, BI and MI are shown read-only and AV writable from the object types and the limit ranges.
Refrigerant points are grouped per barrel and circuit (B1:C1 ... B2:C3), so instance numbers have gaps.
Points for the chiller pumping module, waterside economizer, evaporative condenser and vestibules report only when fitted.
Binary input descriptions are the guide's value type column (Status, Alarm, Fault, Warning, Lockout).

source.title: Main DX Barrel Chiller Controller Technical Guide

integration.summary: Connect the on-board MS/TP port and set MAC address, device ID and baud on the LCD. The BAS runs the chiller with AV 81 Auto/Run/Off and reads the unit mode, leaving water temperature and alarm status. Leaving water reset limits are AV 1 and AV 2.

minimum_points.name: Reset Unit Lockout { 1 = Reset }
minimum_points.why: Write 1 to reset a unit lockout

integration.enable: AV 81 Auto/Run/Off Command (0 = Auto, 1 = Run, 2 = Off) runs the chiller from the BAS; BI 1 shows the Run/Stop input and BI 6/7 the barrel disable commands. AV 80 resets a unit lockout.
setup: MAC address, device ID (up to seven digits) and MS/TP baud rate are set on the controller's LCD BACnet screens.
gotchas: AV 82-91 switch main board relays and set analog output voltages directly; leave them alone unless the BAS is meant to drive those outputs.
